Subject: Annual commit tiers: Starter / Growth / Enterprise proposal for Sequoia Health

Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion, attached is a concise annual commit proposal that maps to three operational profiles we see customers adopt: Starter, Growth, and Enterprise. The sheet includes suggested token bands, list pricing, and a recommended fallback/overage policy so your engineering team can plan for both steady-state and burst traffic. High-level summary below: 

- Starter: 10M tokens / year — unit price $0.00080 per token (approx. 20% off list). Good for light production + POC.
- Growth: 100M tokens / year — unit price $0.00060 per token (approx. 40% off list). Target for productizing features with predictable volume.
- Enterprise: 500M tokens / year — unit price $0.00045 per token (approx. 55% off list). Best for broad rollout, includes priority capacity and dedicated routing.

Overage policy: automated overage billed monthly at a 20% premium to the committed tier rate; burst capacity can be requested (subject to availability) and priced per-case. Billing cadence is quarterly with a quarterly true-up. We can offer up to 10% token carry-forward year-to-year for unused committed tokens as an option.

I've attached the spreadsheet with line-item math and a sample billing ramp (12-month phasing). Please review and let me know which tier you expect to land in and any procurement constraints (PO timing, internal approvals). If helpful, we can include a one-month POC allowance to validate latencies and developer experience before the commit takes effect.

Next step: if Sept 15 works for a decision, we can target an Oct 1 effective date and have SOW + DocuSign ready.

Thanks,
Ava Chen

Ava —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the spreadsheet. A few quick questions from our procurement and infra teams before we loop legal: 

1) True-ups and move-between-tiers: can we move up mid-year and get prorated pricing immediately? If we move down, is it only at renewal?
2) Minimum commitment: is Starter the minimum for enterprise billing, or can we do a 3-month pilot without committing to 10M/yr?
3) SLA and credits: what’s the SLA, and how do credits accrue if there’s an outage?
4) Embeddings vs generation: do embeddings consume the same per-token unit, or do they have a separate unit price? Our search team will want clarity.
5) POC: curious what the POC allowance would look like operationally — is that a free credit or simply a lower committed tier for the first month?
6) Any flexibility on a migration/implementation credit — we have some upfront engineering work to instrument.

If you can answer inline that would be great. We should also check whether multi-year (24-month) pricing is available — that would help our finance team with forecasting.

Thanks,
Evan Miles
Head of Platform, Sequoia Health
evan@sequoia-health.com

Evan —

Great questions — answers below inline. I'll also share a short one-pager (and the DocuSign link) once we align on the tier.

1) Move-between-tiers: Yes — you can move up at any time. Pricing for the new, higher tier applies pro-rata from the date of change. Moving down is only allowed at renewal (we require 30 days’ notice ahead of the renewal date).

2) Minimum / Pilot: We can do a 3-month pilot without a year commitment. For pilots we usually issue a capped credit (see POC section). If you convert the pilot into an annual commit within the pilot window we can apply a credit equal to the pilot spend toward the first quarter’s invoice.

3) SLA & credits: Our hosted API SLA is 99.9% monthly availability for committed tiers. For incidents breaching SLA we offer tiered service credits: 5% of the monthly invoice for a single occurrence that puts monthly availability below SLA, escalating for repeated breaches (we can surface exact SLO definitions in the SOW).

4) Embeddings pricing: embeddings are billed separately by vector unit — proposed: $0.00020 per vector (search/embedding call). Generation token pricing is separate (the tiers above). If you have heavy embed-based workflows we can model a blended commit.

5) POC allowance: We can include a one-month POC credit capped at $5,000 (applies to demo/validation traffic). If you exceed that during the POC, overage will be billed at the Starter tier rate. If you sign an annual commit during/after the POC we’ll credit the actual POC spend against the committed first quarter.

6) Migration/implementation credit: open to a modest one-time migration credit — for example, a two-month service credit applied after signing for transition assistance (engineering office hours & onboarding). We can make that conditional on a 12-month commit or higher.

Other notes: quarterly true-ups are standard (we settle usage vs committed volumes). Overages billed monthly. Carry-forward is allowed up to 10% of committed tokens year-to-year.

If a multi-year (24-month) commit is appealing we can layer an additional 5% discount on top of the Enterprise pricing (we’d want to lock the rate in the contract).

Next step: if Sept 15 is an acceptable decision target, I’ll get a SOW + DocuSign envelope prepared for your procurement team to review.

Best,
